changes.before: Validate a mixed palette while retaining useful per-field types.
changes.after: Check an object's shape while keeping useful types for each field.

before:
A type annotation gives a variable the declared type. A satisfies expression checks compatibility while retaining the expression's resulting specific type.

Record<Keys, Value> describes object properties: each key named by Keys must have a value compatible with Value. A union of literal keys requires those particular names; Record<string, Value> instead describes string-named properties generally. This is a compile-time type, not a runtime object constructor. A string’s toUpperCase() method returns uppercase text without changing the original string.
satisfies is checked by TypeScript and removed from runtime JavaScript. It does not validate incoming data.
It is not a promise to preserve every literal unchanged. Contextual typing still matters; use precise compiler checks instead of assuming all values remain literal types.

For the exercise, create palette with calm text "mint" and alert tuple [255, 80, 0]. Check it satisfies Record<"calm" | "alert", Paint>, then return the uppercase calm name and the alert's first channel.
The palette must keep calm as text and alert as a three-number tuple. A precise safe annotation can meet that contract without using the same satisfies spelling.
after: Satisfies checks whether a value fits a type without simply replacing it with that whole type. Record<Keys, Value> describes properties with the named keys and allowed value type. It does not create an object.
Satisfies is removed before JavaScript runs. It does not inspect incoming data or freeze the object.
Satisfies does not guarantee that every field keeps its exact literal type. The type used for the check can still help shape the inferred result.
Create palette with calm as the text mint and alert as the tuple [255, 80, 0]. Check it against Record<"calm" | "alert", Paint>. Produce the uppercase calm name and the first alert number.
Calm should remain usable as text. Alert should remain a three-number tuple. A safe, precise written type can also meet these requirements.

before.question: Why can palette.calm.toUpperCase() work after this satisfies check without narrowing calm from Paint?
choices: The checked expression retains calm as a string instead of replacing its type with the whole Paint union
satisfies converts every tuple into text
satisfies inserts a runtime if statement
before.explanation: The compatibility check does not replace each field with the broad union annotation. It preserves the useful field-specific result; no runtime conversion happens.

after.question: Why can calm use toUpperCase after this satisfies check?
choices: Its useful string type is kept
Satisfies turns every tuple into text
Satisfies adds a running if statement
after.explanation: The check keeps the useful field-specific type. It does not convert values.

changes.before: Supported by actual TypeScript 5.9.3 runner. Full compile tests prove required keys, tuple length and string operations; no claim that satisfies freezes values or preserves every literal.
changes.after: The checks cover required keys, tuple length, and text operations. Satisfies does not freeze values or preserve every exact literal.
